subject: Dedicated capacity validation: throughput, streaming & tail-latency next steps
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Tadros <sam.tadros@finlytics.com>, Emily Chen <echen@sre.finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity validation: throughput, streaming & tail-latency next steps

Thanks for a productive call this morning — good to line up the SLOs you care about. Quick recap from Redwood and clear next steps so we can scope a dedicated validation run.

Key goals you confirmed:
- Multi-tenant live traffic: sustained concurrency ~60 active sessions, peak bursts to ~120 concurrent sessions.
- Throughput target (aggregate): ~100k tokens / minute (approx 1.7k tokens/sec) during steady-state; spikes to 2.5k t/s for short bursts.
- Tail latency: 95th < 200ms for first token when streaming; 99th < 450ms for full-turn completion (90% of turns under 300 tokens).
- Streaming: chunked streaming required; client expects first-token within 300ms for 75% of requests.

What we propose from Redwood for the validation run:
1) Two-week dedicated validation window on a reserved pool with production-like traces you provide. We'll run concurrent workloads across model variants (gpt-style open model + 8-bit quantized variant) and two GPU configurations for side-by-side comparison (H100 vs A100).
2) Metrics we will capture: per-token latency distribution, first-byte/first-token latency, per-session concurrency, GPU utilization, KV-cache hit rate with prefix sharing.
3) Deliverables: latency_matrix.csv (by percentile & model variant), KV-cache bench report (pdf), recommended reserved throughput and suggested pool size + expected unit cost with fallbacks.

Immediate asks for your team:
- Provide a 24h representative trace and the workload sample (finlytics-workload-sample.json).
- Confirm data residency (you mentioned US-east) and the list of IP ranges for the validation load generator.
- If procurement will sign a short test addendum, loop in Procurement for the DocuSign step.

Attachments: finlytics-workload-sample.json (sample traces) — please upload full traces to the Drive link when ready.

Proposed next step: schedule the validation window starting Tue 6/22 (we can be flexible). If Tue works, I'll send a formal run plan + Dex access for your SREs to watch metrics.

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Sam Tadros <sam.tadros@finlytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Chen <echen@sre.finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity validation: throughput, streaming & tail-latency next steps

Appreciate the recap, Monica — that matches what we discussed. Two clarifications from our end:

1) Tail vs median: our product team is most concerned about first-byte/first-token tail latency for interactive sessions. Ideally we want 95th <= 150–200ms for first token at steady state; if H100 gets us closer there we should prioritize it.
2) Data residency: correct — validation and any temporary logs must stay in us-east-1. We can provide IP ranges and a sanitized 24h trace (we'll strip PII).

Procurement note: they prefer a two-week paid trial with a capped spend. I'll loop them in after we get your quote for the validation pool.

I'll attach the sanitized trace and a short CSV of traffic cadence (will post to Drive).

Sam
Sam Tadros
Head of Platform Engineering, FinLytics
sam.tadros@finlytics.com | +1 (646) 312-9944

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Tadros <sam.tadros@finlytics.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity validation: throughput, streaming & tail-latency next steps

Thanks — reviewing the targets and the sample cadence, here's a pragmatic starting recommendation for the dedicated pool (pre-validation):

Summary (prelim):
- H100 config: 8 x H100 (80GB) nodes recommended for headroom to meet 95th-first-token ~150–200ms with streaming enabled and KV-cache sharing across sessions. With Redwood continuous batching and prefix caching we expect sustained aggregate throughput ~2.0–2.2k t/s and burst to ~3k t/s for short periods.
- A100 config: alternative is 12 x A100 (40GB) with BF16 + int8 quantization; expected median comparable but tail may be 1.2–1.4x higher than H100 under similar load. Useful if cost is the primary constraint.
- Reserved throughput suggestion: start with a reserved pool capable of 2.5k t/s (sustained headroom), allow burst margin to 3.5k t/s via auto-burst policy.

Notes on assumptions:
- Average turn length ~220 tokens; prefixes exhibit high duplication leading to potential 25–35% KV-cache hit rate in our bench.
- Streaming first-token latency numbers assume client chunk-size <= 256 bytes and network RTT <= 60ms.

I attached a quick latency_matrix.csv (percentile breakdown per GPU/model) and a short kv-cache-bench.pdf that shows expected cost/token delta when hit-rate improves.

If FinLytics wants a short validated quote, Monica can finalize with pricing; otherwise we can run a 48–72h smoke test on the exact traces you share to refine sizing before the full two-week window.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Attachments: latency_matrix.csv, kv-cache-bench.pdf

From: Emily Chen <echen@sre.finlytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Sam Tadros <sam.tadros@finlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity validation: throughput, streaming & tail-latency next steps

Thanks Marcus — the numbers look reasonable. We can provide the sanitized 24h trace to the Drive folder and confirm IP ranges by EOD.

A few quick operational asks:
- Can Redwood provide an option to fall back to a smaller model variant (lower-cost) if we see sustained degradation on primary pools?
- We'll want an SLO runbook for how failovers and rollbacks are executed during the two-week validation.

We'll plan to be available for a 2–3 hour validation kickoff on Tue 6/22 (PDT) — prefer morning.

Emily Chen
SRE Lead | FinLytics
echen@sre.finlytics.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity validation: throughput, streaming & tail-latency next steps

Great — thanks everyone. Confirming action items and owners: 

- FinLytics (Sam / Emily): upload sanitized trace + traffic cadence CSV to the Drive link; confirm IP ranges and legal sign-off for a two-week paid trial (Procurement).
- Redwood (Monica / Marcus / Karthik): finalize a draft validation plan and quote (attached: redwood-dedicated-quote-v1.pdf). Marcus will prepare the smoke-test config and latency_matrix for the kickoff.
- Logistics: validation kickoff Tue 2027-06-22 @ 09:00 PDT (we'll send calendar invite shortly).

Key guardrails we agreed on: data residency will be strictly us-east-1 for the validation; Redwood will provide a rollback path and automatic fallback policy to a lower-capacity model variant if tail latencies exceed defined thresholds for >5 minutes. We'll capture traces for post-mortem and retention limited to the test window.

If Procurement is OK with the DocuSign test addendum (link below), we can start provisioning next Monday and be ready for kickoff on Tue.
